Topic: Understanding Discrete Convolutions: From Filters to Features

Target audience: University students (Computer Science/Engineering)

Section: section_1 — Intuitive Hook: The Sliding Window

Lecture lines:
Imagine a filter sliding across an image.
It acts like a magnifying glass for features.
Discrete convolution multiplies and sums local pixels.
We flip the kernel then slide across.
This process systematically discovers hidden patterns.

Planned animations:
Fade in a 3x3 grid (representing a window) over an image array. Color: #FFFFFF.
Highlight the center cell of the window. Color: #FF0000.
Animate the grid sliding one step to the right. Color: #00FF00.
Demonstrate the window capture of pixel values. Color: #FFFF00.
Fade out the entire sliding window demonstration. Color: #FFFFFF.

Section: section_2 — Mathematical Mechanics: The Dot Product

Lecture lines:
Calculate the dot product for each window.
Multiply corresponding kernel and pixel values.
Sum these products to get one output.

Planned animations:
Display the dot product formula MathTex: Sum(I * K). Color: #FFFFFF.
Animate multiplying corresponding elements in the window and kernel. Color: #00FFFF.
Sum these values together into a single scalar value. Color: #00FF00.
Highlight the resulting pixel value transition. Color: #FF00FF.
Show the final scalar value placement in the output. Color: #FFFFFF.

Section: section_3 — Prerequisite Visuals: The Kernel's Identity

Lecture lines:
Kernels are small matrices extracting features.
Blur kernels average out neighboring pixels.
Edge kernels highlight high-contrast boundaries.

Planned animations:
Display a 3x3 identity matrix Kernel: [[0,0,0],[0,1,0],[0,0,0]]. Color: #FFFFFF.
Simulate the sliding window passing through the kernel. Color: #00FFFF.
Highlight that output matches the input perfectly. Color: #00FF00.

Section: section_4 — Real-World Application: Image Processing

Lecture lines:
Convolution forms the backbone of vision.
Stacks of layers recognize complex shapes.
Robots use these to identify obstacles.

Planned animations:
Display a blurred image next to a sharp image. Color: #FFFFFF.
Animate a Gaussian kernel overlaying the sharp image. Color: #FFFF00.
Show the image becoming blurred due to kernel processing. Color: #FF0000.

Section: section_5 — Summary and Synthesis

Lecture lines:
Convolution is sliding, multiplying, and summing.
It bridges raw data to intelligence.
Now you can discover features everywhere.

Planned animations:
Show a recap of the sliding window mechanism. Color: #FFFFFF.
Visualize the convolution operation cycle summary. Color: #00FF00.
Display final takeaway: Kernels define output features. Color: #FFFF00.

    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE

        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

                y = 2.2 - i * 1

        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]

        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Summary and Synthesis", [
            "Convolution is sliding, multiplying, and summing.", 
            "It bridges raw data to intelligence.", 
            "Now you can discover features everywhere."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show a recap of the sliding window mechanism
        # Grid representation: 3x3 filter sliding over 5x5 data
        window = Square(side_length=0.8, color=WHITE)
        grid_viz = VGroup(*[Square(side_length=0.4) for _ in range(25)]).arrange_in_grid(rows=5, cols=5, buff=0)
        self.place_in_area(grid_viz, 'B2', 'D4')
        self.place_at_grid(window, 'C3')
        
        self.play(FadeIn(grid_viz), Create(window))
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFFFFF"))
        self.play(window.animate.shift(RIGHT*0.4))
        self.play(window.animate.shift(DOWN*0.4))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Visualize the convolution operation cycle summary
        bridge_icon = Star(color=GREEN, fill_opacity=0.5)
        self.place_in_area(bridge_icon, 'B5', 'D6')
        
        self.play(GrowFromCenter(bridge_icon))
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FF00"))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Display final takeaway: Kernels define output features
        feature_label = Text("Kernels define Features", font_size=24, color=YELLOW)
        self.place_at_grid(feature_label, 'E3')
        
        self.play(Write(feature_label))
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"))
        self.wait(2)
